subject.title: [Feature]: Add optional capability descriptors to tool definitions

question: What canonical tool-capability taxonomy and trust semantics should OpenClaw expose to plugin policy/audit consumers?
rationale: The requested fields become public Plugin SDK and security-policy inputs, overlap adjacent capability/provenance issues, and require maintainer choices about self-declared plugin metadata versus host-authoritative policy facts.

options.title: Approve Unified Descriptor Contract
options.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics, thread them through tool definitions, plugin metadata, inventory, Gateway protocol, and hook events, and document that declarations do not bypass host policy.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Capability Permissions
options.body: Keep this issue blocked behind the broader manifest grant/default-deny work so descriptors ship only as part of an enforceable capability subsystem.

options.title: Keep As Security Matrix Input Only
options.body: Use the Security Matrix/audit model as the canonical consumer and avoid adding a general-purpose public descriptor field until that PR lands and owners approve the vocabulary.

recommendation.title: Approve Unified Descriptor Contract
recommendation.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics, thread them through tool definitions, plugin metadata, inventory, Gateway protocol, and hook events, and document that declarations do not bypass host policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged host-hook foundation owns the closest SDK seam for trusted policies and tool metadata, and the decision primarily extends that surface.
